claims.text: Machine-learning models using Holder means of elemental and structural properties can improve the accuracy of melting-temperature predictions for high-entropy alloys.
Such machine-learning models can improve the computational efficiency of melting-temperature prediction for high-entropy alloys.
Such machine-learning models can improve prediction of melting properties other than melting temperature.
Relevant elemental descriptors include Holder means of group numbers, atomic radii, and electronegativity.
Relevant structural descriptors include cohesive energy and density.
Machine-learning models based on these descriptors can predict the shear modulus of disordered high-entropy alloys with good accuracy.
Machine-learning models based on these descriptors can predict the bulk modulus of disordered high-entropy alloys with good accuracy.
The demonstrated ability to predict shear and bulk moduli can be extended to prediction of melting temperature and other melting properties.
The proposed melting-property model should remain valid at room temperature and elevated temperatures.
The proposed model should apply across varying high-entropy-alloy compositions.
The proposed model will outperform conventional CALPHAD and first-principles approaches in both accuracy and computational efficiency for melting-property prediction.
First-principles calculations are a conventional alternative to the proposed machine-learning approach.
The model's validity may be limited to particular high-entropy-alloy compositions and structures.
Training on ordered compounds may limit model accuracy and generalizability for disordered high-entropy alloys.
